stage: S1 — criterion validity for stationarity_pf (ADMM stabilization track)
status: FROZEN SPECIFICATION — written and hashed BEFORE the analysis is run
scope: diagnose only. No tolerance, criterion, rho or parameter may be changed. Zero solves, ENFORCED by SolveProfileGuard in blocking mode (CLAUDE.md rule six), never asserted. The prior-art branch survey is read-only: no checkout of the working tree, no merge.

mechanism_under_test.statement: The pf dual residual scales linearly with rho and is compared against a FIXED ABSOLUTE tolerance, so raising rho_pf to tighten primal consensus inflates the stationarity residual by the same factor. The lever and the yardstick are coupled.

code.dual_residual_v: shared_resources_planning.py:4897 — normalized_dual_residual = rho * abs(current - previous) / interface_v_base
code.dual_residual_pf: shared_resources_planning.py:4938 — normalized_dual_residual = rho * abs(current - previous) / interface_rating
code.ratio: shared_resources_planning.py:2454 — dual_pf_mean_ratio = residual_metrics['dual']['pf_mean'] / admm_parameters.tol['stationarity']['pf'] (residual OVER tolerance)
code.binding: p510_e_criteria.py:132 — binding = min(slacks), i.e. the criterion with the LEAST slack

mechanism_under_test.direction_established_before_prediction: slack = tolerance / residual, and residual is proportional to rho, so a HIGHER rho_pf must LOWER the stationarity_pf slack. The sign is read from the code above, not assumed.
mechanism_under_test.what_is_and_is_not_wrong: The formula rho*(z^k - z^{k-1}) is the standard ADMM dual residual (Boyd et al.). What is questionable is pairing a rho-scaled residual with an ABSOLUTE tolerance; standard treatments use relative tolerances scaled by problem data and adapt rho by residual balancing to keep primal and dual residuals commensurate.

primary_artifacts.rule: re-derive from the primary per-cycle artifacts, not from the P5.10-E summary (P5.12-Z convention)
primary_artifacts.cross_check: the re-derived stationarity_pf slacks must reproduce the 93 binding_slack values in data/SRP1/Results/P510/p510_e_criteria.json on the cycles where stationarity_pf is the binding criterion; a mismatch invalidates the analysis

P1_increment_invariance.quantity: g = dual_pf_mean / rho_pf, which by the code equals the mean of abs(current - previous)/interface_rating — the iterate increment alone, with rho divided out
P1_increment_invariance.prediction: if the criterion is rho-dominated, g is approximately INVARIANT across rho_pf in {300, 500, 1000}; if instead the iterates fully compensate, g scales as 1/rho and the residual is invariant
P1_increment_invariance.report: median g per setting, and the ratios g(500)/g(300) and g(1000)/g(300)

P2_slack_scaling.quantity: median stationarity_pf slack per rho setting
P2_slack_scaling.prediction: slack(1000)/slack(300) ≈ 300/1000 = 0.300 exactly IF the increments are unchanged; the observed departure from 0.300 measures how much the iterates compensate

predeclared_outcomes.rho_dominated: ratio in [0.25, 0.40] — the mechanism is confirmed: the criterion moves with the parameter meant to fix it
predeclared_outcomes.compensating: ratio in [0.85, 1.15] — the mechanism is absent: increments shrink in proportion and the criterion is rho-invariant
predeclared_outcomes.partial: anything else — quantify the exponent p in slack ~ rho^(-p) by least squares on log-log, and report p with its three points

predeclared_predictions.P3_matched_index: the three runs have different lengths (18/27/48), so the comparison is made BOTH at matched cycle indices over the common range 1..18 AND over each full trajectory; both are reported, and a material disagreement between them is itself a finding

additional_questions.Q1_trend: within each rho setting, is the stationarity_pf slack approaching 1 (satisfaction), static, or falling? Report the log-slack-versus-cycle slope and the terminal slack.
additional_questions.Q2_commensurability: is an absolute stationarity tolerance commensurate with objective_tolerance = max(1e3, 1e-3 * recourse), which is relative? Report the stationarity tolerance actually in force (derivable as dual_pf_mean / dual_pf_mean_ratio) and state the mismatch in kind, not merely in magnitude.
additional_questions.Q3_aggregation: consensus criteria use BOTH a max and a mean per family, while stationarity uses only dual_<group>_mean_ratio. Report whether a max-based stationarity measure exists in the artifacts and how it would compare.

scope_limit_predeclared.statement: All 93 cycles have the same binding criterion, so the dataset contains NO counterexample. It cannot support any claim about what distinguishes a binding criterion from a non-binding one — only a characterisation of the binding criterion's own behaviour.
scope_limit_predeclared.shape: the same selection-on-success limitation as the P5.12-W/X/Y breadth probe
scope_limit_predeclared.why_the_rho_test_survives_it: P1 and P2 are WITHIN-criterion comparisons across parameter settings, not BETWEEN-criteria comparisons, so they are unaffected by the absence of a counterexample

prior_art_survey.rationale: the residual-balancing branches address exactly the mechanism above, so the survey and this finding are one thread
prior_art_survey.method: read-only: git log --full-history, git show, git diff against the merge base. No checkout, no merge.
prior_art_survey.report: for each branch — what was tried, what the commit messages claim, whether any evaluation artifact exists, and whether it bears on the rho/tolerance coupling
prior_art_survey.limit: commit messages are claims, not evidence; absence of an evaluation artifact must be reported as such

not_permitted: changing any tolerance, criterion, rho or parameter
proposing or running a lever — S1 reports and stops
any between-criteria discrimination claim from this dataset
decision_rule: the analysis stands or falls on P1 and P2 as predeclared above; the prediction is recorded before the numbers are computed, in the manner of the cl_nom/k prediction in P5.13-D gate v2
